summary: 78 items audited. Coverage of mainstream pressed oils, animal fats, ghee variants, shortenings, margarine and cooking sprays is good. The biggest structural problem is that two of the most common modern cooking oils — avocado oil and coconut oil — exist ONLY as cooking-spray entries: the clean ids 'avocado-oil' and 'coconut-oil' are both named '... cooking spray' and parented to 'cooking-spray', so there is no plain liquid avocado oil or coconut oil base item at all. As a knock-on, 'coconut-oil-refined' is parented to the spray. Several ids are over-generic ('neutral', 'pure', 'oil-light', 'cold-pressed', 'bitter', 'styrian', 'cow', 'buffalo', 'tub', 'canola', 'non-hydrogenated', 'butter-flavor', 'butter-flavored') though their display names are fine. 'bitter almond oil' wrongly inherits the plain almond-oil aliases. Notable global gaps: clarified butter, suet vs tallow split, red palm / palm kernel oil, palm shortening, tea-seed (camellia) oil, perilla, argan, niger/ramtil, black-seed (nigella) oil, wheat-germ oil, apricot-kernel oil, poppyseed oil, tigernut oil, brown butter, chili/garlic infused oils, stick margarine, and toasted sesame oil as its own item. Expansion proposed liberally and globally (40 new items).
issues: MAJOR: id 'avocado-oil' is named 'avocado oil cooking spray' and parented to 'cooking-spray'. There is no plain liquid avocado oil in the catalog despite it being a top-tier modern cooking oil. Recommend renaming this id's display to a spray-specific name (or re-id'ing it) and adding a real 'avocado oil' base item.

MAJOR: id 'coconut-oil' is named 'coconut oil cooking spray' and parented to 'cooking-spray'. There is no plain coconut oil base item. Worse, 'coconut-oil-refined' is parented to this SPRAY ('coconut-oil') rather than to a real coconut-oil base. Hierarchy is broken.
'coconut-oil-refined' parent should be a real coconut oil base, not the cooking spray. Currently parentIds=['coconut-oil'] which is the spray.

'bitter' (bitter almond oil) carries aliases ['almond oils', "huile d'amande"] copied from almond-oil. These are wrong — they describe sweet/plain almond oil, not bitter almond oil, and collide with almond-oil's own aliases.

Over-generic / opaque ids that don't reflect their item: 'neutral' (neutral oil), 'pure' (pure oil), 'oil-light' (oil light), 'cold-pressed' (cold pressed pecan oil), 'bitter' (bitter almond oil), 'styrian' (styrian pumpkin seed oil), 'cow' (cow ghee), 'buffalo' (buffalo ghee), 'tub' (tub margarine), 'canola' (canola cooking spray), 'non-hydrogenated' (non hydrogenated shortening), 'butter-flavor' (butter flavor cooking spray), 'butter-flavored' (butter flavored shortening). Display names are acceptable; ids are bad and collision-prone.

'pure oil', 'oil light', 'neutral oil' are vague filler entries (likely dataset-extraction artifacts from labels like 'pure vegetable oil' / 'light olive oil'). 'oil-light' especially is ambiguous — 'light' on an oil label means light in flavor/color, not calories. Consider whether these add value or just noise.

'sesame-oil' folds 'toasted sesame oil' in as an alias, but toasted (dark) sesame oil and plain (light) sesame oil are culinarily distinct (finishing vs cooking). Toasted sesame oil deserves its own child item.
'palm-oil' uses 'red palm oil' as an alias, but red (unrefined) palm oil and refined palm oil are meaningfully different (color, flavor, carotene). Red palm oil deserves its own child.
'avocado-oil' (the spray) carries alias 'oil spray' which is far too generic and would mis-match many sprays; it belongs (if anywhere) on the 'cooking-spray' parent, not on the avocado item.
'tallow' lists 'suet' as an alias, but suet (raw hard fat around kidneys) and tallow (rendered) are distinct in cooking (e.g. British puddings/pastry use raw suet). Suet should be its own item.

'olive-oil' overloads many distinct concepts in aliases: 'evoo'/'extra virgin olive oil'/'virgin olive oil' (grades) plus brand/spray terms 'pam', 'aerosol oil'. The spray/brand aliases ('pam', 'aerosol oil') belong on cooking-spray, not on olive oil; and EVOO is arguably its own child item.

Animal-fat default storage is inconsistent: 'lard', 'duck-fat', 'goose-fat', 'bacon-drippings', 'schmaltz', 'margarine' default to Refrigerated (correct), but 'beef-tallow', 'mutton-tallow' and base 'tallow' default to Pantry. Rendered tallow is shelf-stable so Pantry is defensible, but the inconsistency with lard (also renderable/shelf-stable) is worth a deliberate decision.

'avocado-oil' / 'coconut-oil' (sprays) and other sprays use the generic oil freshness [180,365] or [365,730]; pressurized aerosol sprays generally last longer unopened — consider aligning all sprays to the cooking-spray baseline [365,1095].

CROSS-CATEGORY: 'clarified butter' already exists as id 'clarified' in 'Dairy & Eggs', and 'chili oil' exists as id 'chili-oil' in 'Condiments & Sauces'. Both are arguably fats and might be expected here; not adding duplicates, but flag for a cross-category placement decision. 'clarified' in Dairy & Eggs has aliases=null and could absorb the ghee-vs-clarified-butter distinction.
redundancies: 'mustard oil refined' has identical freshness, storage, tags and no distinguishing aliases vs base 'mustard oil'; refined-vs-unrefined split only adds value if both sides exist (there is no 'mustard oil unrefined'). Either add the unrefined sibling or fold this into the base.
'pumpkin seed oil refined' duplicates base pumpkin seed oil with no unrefined sibling and identical data; redundant unless an unrefined variant is added.

'coconut oil refined' is parented to the coconut-oil SPRAY and there is no coconut-oil base or unrefined sibling, so it currently reads as a redundant near-duplicate of a spray. Resolve by creating a real coconut oil base (see newItems) and re-parenting.

'bitter almond oil' shares almond-oil's exact aliases and freshness; aliases are wrong (see issues). Distinct ingredient but the data overlap makes it look redundant — needs alias cleanup, not deletion.
'pure oil' duplicates generic 'oil' (same freshness/tags, empty aliases). Likely a label artifact ('pure vegetable oil'); candidate for removal or merge.
'oil light' duplicates generic 'oil' with an ambiguous name; candidate for removal or merge.
'neutral oil' overlaps heavily with generic 'oil' (a neutral oil IS just any flavorless cooking oil). Useful as a recipe-matching alias bucket but borderline redundant as a standalone item.

'vanaspati vegetable ghee' and 'vegetable ghee' share the alias 'dalda' and 'vegetable ghees'; vanaspati IS the technical name for hydrogenated vegetable ghee/Dalda. They are effectively the same product — consider making one the alias of the other rather than two near-identical items.

newItems.name: avocado oil
newItems.notes: MAJOR gap. Currently only exists as a cooking spray ('avocado-oil' id). High-smoke-point modern staple. Refined ~12-18mo unopened, unrefined ~6-12mo; [180,365] Pantry matches catalog's generic oil baseline.

newItems.name: coconut oil
newItems.notes: MAJOR gap. Plain solid/liquid coconut oil missing as base; only the spray and a 'refined' child (mis-parented to the spray) exist. Highly stable saturated fat, long shelf life; 'coconut-oil-refined' should be re-parented here.

newItems.name: toasted sesame oil
newItems.notes: Currently only an alias on sesame-oil, but toasted/dark sesame oil is a distinct finishing oil across East Asian cooking vs light sesame oil for cooking.

newItems.name: extra virgin olive oil
newItems.notes: Highest olive oil grade; currently only an alias on olive-oil. Distinct in flavor/price/use (finishing vs cooking).

newItems.name: olive pomace oil
newItems.notes: Existing 'pomace oil' is parented to generic 'oil' and unqualified; pomace oil is specifically an olive byproduct. Either re-parent the existing item under olive oil or add this clearer entry.

newItems.name: brown butter
newItems.notes: Cooked butter with toasted milk solids retained; perishable unlike ghee. Common pastry/sauce fat. Not dairy-free/vegan.

newItems.name: red palm oil
newItems.notes: Unrefined, carotene-rich red palm oil is a staple in West African and Brazilian cooking; distinct from refined palm oil. Currently only an alias on palm-oil.

newItems.name: palm kernel oil
newItems.notes: Extracted from the palm seed (not pulp); higher saturated fat, distinct from palm oil. Used in West African cooking and confectionery.

newItems.name: suet
newItems.notes: Raw hard fat from around the kidneys; distinct from rendered tallow. Essential to British puddings/pastry. Currently only a (misleading) alias on tallow.

newItems.name: palm shortening
newItems.notes: Common non-hydrogenated shortening (paleo/keto baking); distinct from generic and butter-flavored shortening.

newItems.name: stick margarine
newItems.notes: Firmer baking margarine; sibling to existing 'tub margarine'. Completes the tub/stick split.

newItems.name: tea seed oil
newItems.notes: Primary cooking oil in southern China (Hunan) and Japan (tsubaki); high smoke point. From Camellia oleifera — not to be confused with existing camelina oil.

newItems.name: perilla oil
newItems.notes: Korean/Japanese omega-3-rich finishing oil; perishable like flaxseed, prefers fridge.

newItems.name: argan oil
newItems.notes: Moroccan culinary (toasted) argan oil for finishing/amlou. Tree nut (argan kernel) — not Nut-Free.

newItems.name: mustard oil unrefined
newItems.notes: Completes the refined/unrefined split for mustard oil (mustard-oil-refined already exists). Overlaps conceptually with existing 'kachi ghani (cold-pressed)' — reconcile so kachi ghani is an alias of this rather than a separate opaque item.

newItems.name: niger seed oil
newItems.notes: Edible oil used in Ethiopian (noog) and Indian (ramtil) cooking. Global gap.

newItems.name: black seed oil
newItems.notes: Nigella sativa oil, used in Middle Eastern/South Asian cooking and as a supplement.

newItems.name: wheat germ oil
newItems.notes: Vitamin-E-rich finishing oil; highly perishable, fridge-preferred. Wheat-derived — NOT Gluten-Free.

newItems.name: apricot kernel oil
newItems.notes: Mild nutty oil for dressings/baking; kernel/stone-fruit nut — not Nut-Free.

newItems.name: poppyseed oil
newItems.notes: Delicate European/Indian salad and baking oil.

newItems.name: tigernut oil
newItems.notes: From chufa tubers (a tuber, not a true nut, so Nut-Free); Spanish/West African use.

newItems.name: garlic oil
newItems.notes: Home-infused garlic oil is a botulism risk at room temp, so Refrigerated with a short window. Commercial acidified versions last longer but conservative default is safest.

newItems.name: lemon olive oil
newItems.notes: Citrus-infused finishing olive oil, common in Mediterranean cooking and gift sets.

newItems.name: schmaltz with gribenes
newItems.notes: Schmaltz rendered with crispy skin/fat bits (gribenes); Ashkenazi staple. Shorter life due to solids.

newItems.name: pork fatback
newItems.notes: Unrendered pork back fat used for larding, charcuterie, cooking. Distinct from rendered 'back fat lard' already in catalog.

newItems.name: leaf lard
newItems.notes: Premium lard rendered from the soft fat around the kidneys; prized for flaky pastry. Distinct quality grade from generic lard.

newItems.name: extra virgin coconut oil
newItems.notes: Unrefined coconut oil with coconut aroma; completes the refined/virgin split alongside the existing 'coconut oil refined' once a coconut-oil base exists.

newItems.name: high-oleic sunflower oil
newItems.notes: High-stability frying oil; currently only an alias on sunflower-oil. Distinct shelf life/use.

newItems.name: blended vegetable oil
newItems.notes: Common multi-seed retail blend (e.g. canola+sunflower); broadly used global frying staple.

newItems.name: duck fat cooking spray
newItems.notes: Aerosol duck fat spray (popular for roasting); complements existing animal-fat and spray entries.

newItems.name: vegetable oil cooking spray
newItems.notes: Generic veg-oil aerosol (the most common PAM-style spray); the catalog has olive/canola/coconut/avocado/butter sprays but no plain vegetable one.

newItems.name: baking spray with flour
newItems.notes: Cooking spray with added flour for cake pans; contains flour so NOT Gluten-Free.

newItems.name: lardo
newItems.notes: Italian cured/seasoned pork back fat eaten as a fat/charcuterie; distinct from fresh fatback and rendered lard.

newItems.name: yak butter
newItems.notes: Tibetan/Himalayan butter used in butter tea and cooking; global animal-fat gap. Dairy so not vegan/dairy-free.

newItems.name: smen
newItems.notes: North African fermented/aged clarified butter, shelf-stable. Distinct from ghee/clarified butter by fermentation.

newItems.name: kokum butter
newItems.notes: Indian plant fat (Garcinia indica) used in confectionery and some cooking; very stable. Global plant-fat gap.

newItems.name: shea butter (food grade)
newItems.notes: Food-grade shea is used as a cooking/baking fat in West Africa and as a cocoa-butter equivalent. Stable plant fat.

Re-parent from the spray ('coconut-oil') to the new plain coconut oil base item.

Remove inherited aliases ['almond oils', "huile d'amande"] (they belong to plain almond oil). Add correct aliases like ['bitter almond essence oil', 'amande amère']. Consider re-id to 'bitter-almond-oil'. Note bitter almond oil is typically a flavoring, not a bulk cooking fat.
Remove 'toasted sesame oil' from aliases now that toasted sesame oil is a distinct child item; keep light/raw sesame aliases on the base.
Remove 'red palm oil' from aliases now that red palm oil is its own child; keep refined-palm aliases on base.
Remove 'suet' alias (suet is raw, not rendered) now that suet is its own item; add 'beef dripping'/'dripping' instead.

Trim grade/brand/spray overload: move 'pam' and 'aerosol oil' to cooking-spray; with EVOO now a child item, decide whether to keep 'evoo'/'extra virgin olive oil' as base aliases or only on the child.

Reconcile with the proposed 'mustard oil unrefined': kachi ghani IS cold-pressed (unrefined) mustard oil. Make one the canonical item and the other an alias rather than two opaque entries.
Resolve overlap with 'vanaspati': vanaspati is the technical name for hydrogenated vegetable ghee/Dalda. Merge into one item with the other name as an alias; they currently share 'dalda'.
Opaque id 'neutral' for 'neutral oil'. Either re-id to 'neutral-oil', or demote to an alias bucket on generic 'oil' if it isn't pulling its weight as a standalone item.

'oil light' is ambiguous (light flavor/color, not calories) and duplicates generic 'oil'. Recommend removal, merge, or rename to 'light olive oil' if that was the intent.

Opaque id 'cold-pressed' for 'cold pressed pecan oil'. Re-id to 'pecan-oil-cold-pressed'. Note it overlaps heavily with the existing 'pecan oil unrefined' — reconcile (cold-pressed pecan oil IS unrefined).
